title: 3D Turf War
statementMd:
In a four-dimensional world, video games would take place on three-dimensional screens in the same way we humans play video games on two-dimensional screens. There are k𝑘 four-dimensional beings playing their favorite game on an m×n×h𝑚×𝑛×ℎ grid. Each player has their own color.

The game has r𝑟 turns. Each turn results in some player coloring a rectangular prism subgrid with their color. If any of these cells had been previously colored, they are overwritten to have the new color.

Formally, a turn is defined by a player number i𝑖 and two triples (x1,y1,z1)(𝑥1,𝑦1,𝑧1) and (x2,y2,z2)(𝑥2,𝑦2,𝑧2), where x1≤x2𝑥1≤𝑥2; y1≤y2𝑦1≤𝑦2; and z1≤z2𝑧1≤𝑧2. Player i𝑖 colors all (x,y,z)(𝑥,𝑦,𝑧) such that x1≤x≤x2𝑥1≤𝑥≤𝑥2; y1≤y≤y2; and z1≤z≤z2. Below is an example of a turn for m=4,n=3,h=2. The player has colored the subgrid defined by corners (0,0,0) and (2,1,1).

![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/6319a3caf45d62d37f14cb9d9762993193da9417.png)

Your task is to calculate, at the end of the game, how many cells in the grid were only ever colored by one player. Note that a cell might get colored by the same player multiple times across different turns.

## Input

Each test contains multiple test cases. The first line contains the number of test cases t (1≤t≤50). The description of the test cases follows.

The first line of each test case consists of five integers, m, n, h, k and r (1≤mnh,k,r≤4⋅105) — this represents a k-player game lasting r turns played on an m×n×h grid.

The next r lines of each test case consist of seven integers each: i,x1,y1,z1,x2,y2,z2 (0≤i,x1,y1,z1,x2,y2,z2<4⋅105). The following conditions are guaranteed: i<k; x1≤x2<m; y1≤y2<n; and z1≤z2<h. This line represents a turn in which player number i colors the entire subgrid defined by (x1,y1,z1) and (x2,y2,z2).

It is guaranteed that the sum of mnh over all test cases is at most 4⋅105 and the sum of r over all test cases is at most 4⋅105.

## Output

For each test case, output a single integer — the number of cells in the grid that were only ever colored by exactly one player.

## Note

In the first test case, there are two players and three turns. Here are the game states after each turn.

![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/6319a3caf45d62d37f14cb9d9762993193da9417.png) ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/73856186fa604674535d229933dcebe6d6789208.png)

The changes to the state after the third move are not visible from the previous angle, so a rotated view is below.

![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/5c5833356ca47eb723b1177cf1166f9227e52abf.png)

In total, 16 cells were colored over the course of the game. Of these, the five cells {(1,0,0),(1,1,0),(1,2,0),(1,0,1),(1,1,1)} were colored by both players at some point. The other 11 were only touched by one player (10 by the first player and 1 by the second player).
